ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 谷歌在近期针对教育市场的技术更新中明确表示，其推出的Gemini、Gemini Notebook以及AI搜索等核心功能将默认处于关闭状态，学校可根据需求自行选择是否开启。此举旨在回应教育界对学生数据隐私和课堂控制权的长期担忧，试图通过交出选择权来缓解学校对大模型入校的抵触情绪。

This move aims to address growing concerns from educators regarding student data privacy and classroom control.

That is what stayed with me reading about Britain’s 2013 settlement w
viral_ticker_tweets.title_en:
A claim can survive for decades. Evidence cannot.

That is what stayed with me reading about Britain’s 2013 settlement with 5,228 Kenyan claimants over torture and ill-treatment during the colonial Emergency.

The abuses dated back to 1952–1963. By the time the settlement arrived, more than half a century separated the harm from the remedy.

That gap changes more than the calendar.

Witnesses disappear. Records become harder to find. Memory weakens. Delay can start deciding what can still be proved before anyone decides what was right.

That is the justice problem I keep thinking about as AI agents begin making deals at machine speed.

Their disputes may be smaller, but there could be millions of them. A system that resolves them too slowly risks making the evidence harder to assess before the disagreement is settled.

That is where @GenLayer interests me. Independent AI validators review the same evidence and reach a verdict together, in minutes and at a fraction of the cost of a court.

Speed is not just convenience here.

It helps preserve the dispute while the facts are still fresh.

If an AI-agent deal goes wrong, how long should its evidence remain challengeable before the record becomes final?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

虐待行为可以追溯到 1952 年至 1963 年。当和解协议达成时，危害与补救已经相隔半个多世纪了。

这个差距比日历的变化还要大。

目击者消失。记录变得更难找到。记忆力变弱。在任何人决定什么是正确的之前，延迟可以开始决定什么仍然可以被证明。

当人工智能代理开始以机器速度进行交易时，这就是我一直在思考的正义问题。

他们的纠纷可能较小，但可能有数百万起。解决问题速度太慢的系统可能会导致在分歧得到解决之前更难评估证据。

这就是@GenLayer 让我感兴趣的地方。独立的人工智能验证者审查相同的证据并共同做出裁决，只需几分钟，而费用只是法院的一小部分。

在这里，速度不仅仅是方便。

它有助于在事实仍然新鲜的情况下维持争议。

如果人工智能代理交易出了问题，在记录成为最终结果之前，其证据应在多长时间内受到质疑？

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

目击者消失。记录变得更难找到。记忆力变弱。在任何人决定什么是正确的之前，延迟可以开始决定什么仍然可以被证明。

当人工智能代理开始以机器速度进行交易时，这就是我一直在思考的正义问题。

他们的纠纷可能较小，但可能有数百万起。解决问题速度太慢的系统可能会导致在分歧得到解决之前更难评估证据。

这就是@GenLayer 让我感兴趣的地方。独立的人工智能验证者审查相同的证据并共同做出裁决，只需几分钟，而费用只是法院的一小部分。

在这里，速度不仅仅是方便。

它有助于在事实仍然新鲜的情况下维持争议。

如果人工智能代理交易出了问题，在记录成为最终结果之前，其证据应在多长时间内受到质疑？

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

viral_ticker_tweets.content_snippet:
A claim can survive for decades. Evidence cannot.

That is what stayed with me reading about Britain’s 2013 settlement with 5,228 Kenyan claimants over torture and ill-treatment during the colonial Emergency.

The abuses dated back to 1952–1963. By the time the settlement arrived, more than half a century separated the harm from the remedy.

That gap changes more than the calendar.

Witnesses disappear. Records become harder to find. Memory weakens. Delay can start deciding what can still be proved before anyone decides what was right.

That is the justice problem I keep thinking about as AI agents begin making deals at machine speed.

Their disputes may be smaller, but there could be millions of them. A system that resolves them too slowly risks making the evidence harder to assess before the disagreement is settled.

That is where @GenLayer interests me. Independent AI validators review the same evidence and reach a verdict together, in minutes and at a fraction of the cost of a court.

Speed is not just convenience here.

It helps preserve the dispute while the facts are still fresh.

If an AI-agent deal goes wrong, how long should its evidence remain challengeable before the record becomes final?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

viral_ticker_tweets.title:
Republicans earned this humiliation.

Newsflash for the GOP: campaigning on no new wars and lower prices, then starting
viral_ticker_tweets.title_en:
Republicans earned this humiliation.

Newsflash for the GOP: campaigning on no new wars and lower prices, then starting a major war and raising prices, isn’t a good political strategy.

Trump and the Republican Party were handed a generational opportunity in 2024. 

Groups such as MAHA voters and young men, along with growing support among Hispanic and Muslim voters, helped give them a coalition that could have reshaped American politics for a generation.

They squandered it in two years.

What happened tonight is the opposite of political rocket science.

The GOP invited everyone into its “big tent,” then betrayed the people who showed up. 

Broken promises on virtually everything except closing the border. 

What did they expect would happen?

They confused support for their promises with unconditional loyalty to their party. 

They acted like winning an election meant they no longer had to listen to the people who won it for them.

The biggest slap in the face was to MAGA itself. 

Their most loyal supporters were promised a government that would finally put them first. 

Republicans cannot campaign on changing everything, fail to deliver on the things people care about most, and then blame those people for being angry.

The handling of the Epstein files, the promises surrounding DOGE being abandoned, and the endless cycle of big announcements followed with zero change or action only compounded the issue.

You cannot build an entire movement around exposing corruption and demanding accountability, then act offended when your own supporters demand both from you.

What exactly were Republicans asking voters to reward tonight? 

At some point, “the Democrats are worse” stops being a campaign and starts being an admission that you have nothing else to offer.

The Republican Party took an extraordinary political opening and turned it into a case study in arrogance, complacency, and wasted potential.

But you could argue this is the best possible outcome for Republicans before 2028. 

They just received a brutal warning while they still have two years to change course.

If their response is to blame voters, attack critics, and insist everything is going perfectly, they deserve what comes next.

Life after Trump is approaching. 

Republicans have to decide whether they will return to the neocon politics their own voters rejected, remain trapped in defending everything Trump does, or build a party capable of keeping its promises.

Democrats, meanwhile, have just been handed the opportunity Republicans wasted. 

Their biggest mistake would be assuming tonight means voters have embraced every part of the Democratic agenda.

Voters punishing Republicans is not a blank check for Democrats. 

If Democrats spend the next two years indulging their own ideological factions, letting the DSA set the direction, and dismissing concerns about affordability and everyday life, they will make the exact same mistake.

Republicans thought anger at Democrats would spare them from having to deliver. 

Democrats should not be stupid enough to believe anger at Republicans will spare them either.

Neither party owns the people who vote for it. 

Earn their trust, keep your promises, or expect to lose it.

共和党人应受这样的羞辱。

共和党的快讯：在竞选中主张不发动新的战争和降低价格，然后发动一场大规模战争并提高价格，这并不是一个好的政治策略。

2024 年，特朗普和共和党获得了一个世代相传的机会。

MAHA 选民和年轻人等团体，以及西班牙裔和穆斯林选民日益增长的支持，帮助他们建立了一个联盟，该联盟可能重塑一代人的美国政治。

两年之内他们就把它浪费掉了。

今晚发生的事情与政治火箭科学相反。

共和党邀请所有人进入它的“大帐篷”，然后背叛了出现的人。

除了关闭边境之外，几乎所有事情都没有兑现承诺。

他们期望会发生什么？

他们混淆了对自己承诺的支持和对政党的无条件忠诚。

他们表现得好像赢得选举意味着他们不再需要听取为他们赢得选举的人的意见。

最大的一记耳光是打给MAGA自己的。

他们最忠实的支持者得到了一个最终将他们放在第一位的政府的承诺。

共和党人不能在竞选中力图改变一切，未能实现人们最关心的事情，然后指责这些人的愤怒。

爱泼斯坦文件的处理、围绕 DOGE 的承诺被放弃，以及随之而来的无休止的重大公告、零变化或行动，只会让问题变得更加复杂。

你不能围绕揭露腐败和要求问责来发起一场完整的运动，然后当你自己的支持者要求你同时要求你做到这两点时，你又表现得被冒犯了。

共和党人今晚到底要求选民奖励什么？

在某种程度上，“民主党更糟糕”不再是一场竞选活动，而是开始承认你没有其他可提供的。

共和党采取了非同寻常的政治开放，并将其变成了傲慢、自满和浪费潜力的案例研究。

但你可能会说，这是共和党在 2028 年之前可能出现的最佳结果。

他们刚刚收到残酷的警告，而他们还有两年的时间改变路线。

如果他们的反应是指责选民、攻击批评者并坚称一切进展顺利，那么他们就活该承受接下来的后果。

特朗普之后的生活即将到来。

共和党人必须决定是否要回到被自己的选民拒绝的新保守主义政治，还是继续为特朗普所做的一切辩护，还是建立一个能够信守承诺的政党。

与此同时，民主党人刚刚获得了共和党人浪费的机会。

他们最大的错误是假设今晚意味着选民已经接受了民主党议程的各个部分。

选民惩罚共和党并不是民主党的空白支票。

如果民主党人在接下来的两年里放纵自己的意识形态派别，让 DSA 设定方向，并忽视对负担能力和日常生活的担忧，他们就会犯同样的错误。

viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_en:
Republicans earned this humiliation.

Newsflash for the GOP: campaigning on no new wars and lower prices, then starting a major war and raising prices, isn’t a good political strategy.

Trump and the Republican Party were handed a generational opportunity in 2024. 

Groups such as MAHA voters and young men, along with growing support among Hispanic and Muslim voters, helped give them a coalition that could have reshaped American politics for a generation.

They squandered it in two years.

What happened tonight is the opposite of political rocket science.

The GOP invited everyone into its “big tent,” then betrayed the people who showed up. 

Broken promises on virtually everything except closing the border. 

What did they expect would happen?

They confused support for their promises with unconditional loyalty to their party. 

They acted like winning an election meant they no longer had to listen to the people who won it for them.

The biggest slap in the face was to MAGA itself. 

Their most loyal supporters were promised a government that would finally put them first. 

Republicans cannot campaign on changing everything, fail to deliver on the things people care about most, and then blame those people for being angry.

The handling of the Epstein files, the promises surrounding DOGE being abandoned, and the endless cycle of big announcements followed with zero change or action only compounded the issue.

You cannot build an entire movement around exposing corruption and demanding accountability, then act offended when your own supporters demand both from you.

What exactly were Republicans asking voters to reward tonight? 

At some point, “the Democrats are worse” stops being a campaign and starts being an admission that you have nothing else to offer.

The Republican Party took an extraordinary political opening and turned it into a case study in arrogance, complacency, and wasted potential.

But you could argue this is the best possible outcome for Republicans before 2028. 

They just received a brutal warning while they still have two years to change course.

If their response is to blame voters, attack critics, and insist everything is going perfectly, they deserve what comes next.

Life after Trump is approaching. 

Republicans have to decide whether they will return to the neocon politics their own voters rejected, remain trapped in defending everything Trump does, or build a party capable of keeping its promises.

Democrats, meanwhile, have just been handed the opportunity Republicans wasted. 

Their biggest mistake would be assuming tonight means voters have embraced every part of the Democratic agenda.

Voters punishing Republicans is not a blank check for Democrats. 

If Democrats spend the next two years indulging their own ideological factions, letting the DSA set the direction, and dismissing concerns about affordability and everyday life, they will make the exact same mistake.

Republicans thought anger at Democrats would spare them from having to deliver. 

Democrats should not be stupid enough to believe anger at Republicans will spare them either.

Neither party owns the people who vote for it. 

Earn their trust, keep your promises, or expect to lose it.
viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_zh:
共和党人应受这样的羞辱。

共和党的快讯：在竞选中主张不发动新的战争和降低价格，然后发动一场大规模战争并提高价格，这并不是一个好的政治策略。

2024 年，特朗普和共和党获得了一个世代相传的机会。

MAHA 选民和年轻人等团体，以及西班牙裔和穆斯林选民日益增长的支持，帮助他们建立了一个联盟，该联盟可能重塑一代人的美国政治。

两年之内他们就把它浪费掉了。

今晚发生的事情与政治火箭科学相反。

共和党邀请所有人进入它的“大帐篷”，然后背叛了出现的人。

除了关闭边境之外，几乎所有事情都没有兑现承诺。

他们期望会发生什么？

他们混淆了对自己承诺的支持和对政党的无条件忠诚。

他们表现得好像赢得选举意味着他们不再需要听取为他们赢得选举的人的意见。

最大的一记耳光是打给MAGA自己的。

他们最忠实的支持者得到了一个最终将他们放在第一位的政府的承诺。

共和党人不能在竞选中力图改变一切，未能实现人们最关心的事情，然后指责这些人的愤怒。

爱泼斯坦文件的处理、围绕 DOGE 的承诺被放弃，以及随之而来的无休止的重大公告、零变化或行动，只会让问题变得更加复杂。

你不能围绕揭露腐败和要求问责来发起一场完整的运动，然后当你自己的支持者要求你同时要求你做到这两点时，你又表现得被冒犯了。

共和党人今晚到底要求选民奖励什么？

在某种程度上，“民主党更糟糕”不再是一场竞选活动，而是开始承认你没有其他可提供的。

共和党采取了非同寻常的政治开放，并将其变成了傲慢、自满和浪费潜力的案例研究。

但你可能会说，这是共和党在 2028 年之前可能出现的最佳结果。

他们刚刚收到残酷的警告，而他们还有两年的时间改变路线。

如果他们的反应是指责选民、攻击批评者并坚称一切进展顺利，那么他们就活该承受接下来的后果。

特朗普之后的生活即将到来。

共和党人必须决定是否要回到被自己的选民拒绝的新保守主义政治，还是继续为特朗普所做的一切辩护，还是建立一个能够信守承诺的政党。

与此同时，民主党人刚刚获得了共和党人浪费的机会。

他们最大的错误是假设今晚意味着选民已经接受了民主党议程的各个部分。

选民惩罚共和党并不是民主党的空白支票。

如果民主党人在接下来的两年里放纵自己的意识形态派别，让 DSA 设定方向，并忽视对负担能力和日常生活的担忧，他们就会犯同样的错误。

共和党人认为对民主党人的愤怒会让他们不必兑现承诺。

民主党人不应该愚蠢到相信对共和党人的愤怒也会让他们幸免。

任何一方都不拥有投票给它的人。

赢得他们的信任，信守承诺，否则就会失去信任。

top_three.article_content_zh:
此次更新不仅是接口层面的开放，更是苹果对iOS交互逻辑的一次彻底重构。通过赋予Siri跨应用调用的能力，苹果试图将AI直接植入到操作系统的毛细血管中，从而在激烈的AI硬件竞争中守住生态壁垒。

开发者被要求配置特定的“技能包”，这意味着未来Siri将不再只是单纯的听指令，而是能够理解用户在屏幕上所见的内容，并主动关联后台服务。这一举措标志着苹果正在试图通过高度整合的AI中台，反向定义移动操作系统的交互范式。

top_three.title: Rapid LLM development is outrunning the research meant to explain it, study finds
top_three.title_en: Rapid LLM development is outrunning the research meant to explain it, study finds
top_three.author: THE DECODER
top_three.article_content:
Stanford researchers tested 50 widely cited claims about LLMs against 20 current models. 44 percent of the findings are already "expired," and another 34 percent have weakened significantly. The average lifespan is just 15.7 months. Claims about what models can't do expire fastest.

The article Rapid LLM development is outrunning the research meant to explain it, study finds appeared first on The Decoder.
top_three.content_snippet:
Stanford researchers tested 50 widely cited claims about LLMs against 20 current models. 44 percent of the findings are already "expired," and another 34 percent have weakened significantly. The average lifespan is just 15.7 months. Claims about what models can't do expire fastest.

The article Rapid LLM development is outrunning the research meant to explain it, study finds appeared first on The Decoder.
top_three.summary_en: Stanford researchers analyzed 50 widely cited claims about LLMs, finding that 44% are obsolete and 34% have significantly weakened, with an average shelf life of just 15.7 months. Claims about model limitations become irrelevant fastest, proving that LLM evolution is outpacing the pace of academic research.
top_three.title_zh: AI研究的寿命竟不足16个月
top_three.summary_zh: 斯坦福研究指出，由于AI迭代过快，近8成关于LLM能力的论文结论在短时间内即告“过期”或失效

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 斯坦福研究人员对比分析了50项关于大语言模型的权威研究，发现约44%的结论已完全失效，34%的结论效力显著减弱，平均有效期仅为15.7个月。其中，关于“模型不能做什么”的论断失效速度最快，反映出AI技术的进化速度已彻底碾压了学术界对其进行解释和归纳的能力。

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 在AI圈发论文简直是在玩‘打地鼠’，前脚刚论证模型智力天花板，后脚就被模型的新版本扇了脸。与其说是科研，不如说是在给不断进化、随时背刺人类常识的数字怪物写遗书。

It’s not so much science as it is writing obituaries for AI capabilities that are constantly evolving to spite us.

news.title: Q&A with Simile CEO Joon Sung Park on claims that its digital twins predict human behavior with 85%+ accuracy, its goal of simulating all 8B people, and more (Mario Gabriele/The Generalist)
news.title_en: Q&A with Simile CEO Joon Sung Park on claims that its digital twins predict human behavior with 85%+ accuracy, its goal of simulating all 8B people, and more (Mario Gabriele/The Generalist)
news.author: The Generalist
news.article_content:
“In any truly advanced civilization that gets depicted [in science fiction], you really see two pillars of scientific progress. One is some form of AGI, and the other a simulation. And I was always more drawn to the idea of simulation.” – Joon Sung Park, Co-Founder and CEO of Simile

Before Joon Sung Park and I had ever met, he simulated the conversation. What questions would Mario, or a person like Mario, ask him? What would I find most interesting to dig into? I do not know how closely I adhered to my facsimile, though I wish I did.

Joon has an advantage in rehearsing these encounters, and thousands of others. He is the Co-founder and CEO of Simile, an applied AI company building a foundation model of human behavior. That involves creating digital twins of real people – like a writer or podcaster – and simulating how they might react to certain circumstances. As you might imagine, that’s an attractive proposition for many companies: CVS Health, for instance, can test a new pricing policy against thousands of simulated patients. A bank can model how customers will react before announcing a fee change. Joon’s ambitions stretch far beyond these cases, though, and Simile has raised more than $300 million, most recently at a $2 billion valuation, to pursue them.

The portrait artist always paints themselves. I loved this line from Joon, who happens to be a gifted painter in his own right. When apprehending a piece of art – whatever the medium – I can sometimes forget to consider what it tells us about the author rather than the subject.

“Emotional rigor.” Another phrase of Joon’s that I’ve been sitting with. This was how he described the intensity one needs to build to paint a beautiful painting of someone. You need to build this deep, rigorous connection. This is a universal lesson, I think, and especially true in writing.

Contradictory superpowers. Another really sharp heuristic (can you tell I enjoyed this conversation quite a lot?). When it comes to hiring, this is what Joon looks for: someone with two strengths that rarely go together. For example, a colleague with deep scientific seriousness and a very playful side.

Working backwards. Joon’s ultimate goal is not to give Simile a question and have it make a prediction. It is to give a “wicked” problem like climate change and have it simulate a superabundance of possible paths to help us find the best one.

Who wins when everything is predictable? If simulation becomes as ubiquitous as Simile suggests it might, how do companies compete with one another? Is “strategy,” as a broad discipline, solved? Joon pointed to a few thoughts on where edge might still live – namely in point of view, proprietary data, and compute. Now, this is just a thought experiment, of course. But two of those three presumably redound to the world’s best-resourced companies, which is far from ideal.

When I asked Joon what book he'd assign to everyone, he named The Catcher in the Rye, which he first read at around 14 or 15. He was careful to say that the books that matter most are deeply personal, but Holden Caulfield's visceral portrait of a young mind stuck with him. Earlier in our conversation, he also pointed to Asimov's Foundation series as a core inspiration for Simile, and particularly the idea of psychohistory: giving a simulator a desired end state and working backwards to find the path there.

Jon Ronson has a new book out, The Castle. I’m only a few pages in, but given that I’ve loved all of his other bizarre, freewheeling investigations, I suspect I’ll like it quite a bit.

Grok Bot is really very good at this point. I suspect this form factor – persistent, proactive, task-specific bots overseen by an orchestrator – will become the default for professional work. It’s the closest thing to having a collection of digital coworkers.

Mario Gabriele: If you can predict the future, then you could be the world’s greatest hedge fund ever.

Joon Sung Park: So it’s a really interesting question. Simile is an applied AI layer that basically allows you to predict people’s behavior at the level of individuals and populations. We can predict people’s behavior with 85% plus accuracy.

Mario Gabriele: And the ultimate goal is to simulate all 8 billion humans and predict the future in some sense?

Joon Sung Park: Yes, it is about representing people in our society and also try to understand the interaction between them. A lot of the companies that we work with, they want to talk to their niche population all the time, but they can maybe, if they’re lucky, to get to talk to them once, but we create simulations of them once, then they can ask them any questions.

news.title_zh: Simile欲用AI数字孪生模拟人类行为
news.summary_zh: Simile公司CEO朴俊圣在访谈中阐述了其开发人类行为基础模型、构建数字孪生以预测人类反应的宏大愿景
news.article_content_zh:
“在[科幻小说中]描绘的任何真正先进的文明中，你确实看到了科学进步的两大支柱。一个是某种形式的通用人工智能，另一个是模拟。而我总是对模拟的想法更感兴趣。” – Joon Sung Park，Simile 联合创始人兼首席执行官

在我和朴俊成见面之前，他就模拟了对话。马里奥或像马里奥这样的人会问他什么问题？我觉得最值得深入研究的是什么？我不知道我对传真的坚持有多严格，尽管我希望如此。

琼在排练这些遭遇以及其他数千场遭遇方面具有优势。他是 Simile 的联合创始人兼首席执行官，Simile 是一家应用人工智能公司，致力于构建人类行为的基础模型。这涉及创建真人（如作家或播客）的数字双胞胎，并模拟他们对某些情况的反应。正如您可能想象的那样，这对许多公司来说是一个有吸引力的提议：例如，CVS Health 可以针对数千名模拟患者测试新的定价政策。银行可以在宣布费用调整之前模拟客户的反应。不过，Joon 的野心远远超出了这些案件，Simile 已筹集了超过 3 亿美元的资金来追求这些目标，最近的估值为 20 亿美元。

肖像画家总是画自己。我喜欢 Joon 的这句话，他本身就是一位有天赋的画家。当理解一件艺术作品时——无论何种媒介——我有时会忘记考虑它告诉我们关于作者而不是主题的信息。

“情感上的严谨。”我一直在听 Joon 的另一句话。他这样描述了为某人画一幅美丽的画所需要的强度。你需要建立这种深刻、严格的联系。我认为这是一个普遍的教训，在写作中尤其如此。

矛盾的超能力。另一个非常尖锐的启发式（你能看出我非常喜欢这次谈话吗？）。在招聘时，Joon 寻找的就是这样的人：具有两种很少同时具备的优势的人。例如，一位有着深厚的科学严肃性和非常顽皮的一面的同事。

向后工作。 Joon 的最终目标不是给 Simile 一个问题并让它做出预测。它是给出一个像气候变化这样的“邪恶”问题，并让它模拟大量可能的路径，以帮助我们找到最好的路径。

当一切都可以预测时谁会获胜？如果模拟像 Simile 所暗示的那样无处不在，那么公司如何相互竞争呢？ “战略”作为一门广泛的学科，是否已得到解决？ Joon 指出了关于边缘可能仍然存在的一些想法——即观点、专有数据和计算。当然，这只是一个思想实验。但这三者中的两家可能会为世界上资源最丰富的公司带来回报，但这远非理想。

当我问 Joon 他会给每个人分配哪本书时，他给大家起名叫《麦田里的守望者》，他第一次读这本书是在 14 或 15 岁左右。他小心翼翼地说，最重要的书都是非常个人化的，但霍尔顿·考尔菲尔德对年轻人内心的描绘却让他印象深刻。在我们谈话的早些时候，他还指出阿西莫夫的基础系列是《Simile》的核心灵感，特别是心理史学的想法：给模拟器一个理想的最终状态，并向后寻找那里的路径。

乔恩·罗森出版了一本新书《城堡》。我只读了几页，但考虑到我喜欢他所有其他奇异、随心所欲的调查，我怀疑我会非常喜欢它。

Grok Bot 在这一点上确实非常出色。我怀疑这种形式因素——由协调者监督的持久、主动、特定任务的机器人——将成为专业工作的默认形式。这是最接近拥有一群数字同事的事情。

news.title: California accepts $1.42B in federal broadband funding, but challenges the Trump administration's demand that it stop enforcing state net neutrality rules (Jon Brodkin/Ars Technica)
news.title_en: California accepts $1.42B in federal broadband funding, but challenges the Trump administration's demand that it stop enforcing state net neutrality rules (Jon Brodkin/Ars Technica)
news.author: Ars Technica
news.article_content:
State tries to obtain broadband funds despite rejecting Trump admin condition.

California is accepting $1.42 billion in broadband grant funding from the Trump administration, but the state is not accepting the Trump administration’s demand that it stop enforcing a net neutrality law and other telecom regulations.

California’s stand against the Trump administration could result in multiple legal battles involving the state, federal government, and Internet providers seeking government funds. Although California told the federal government it would accept the money, it is reserving the right to challenge the condition imposed by the US. The state could delay or cancel plans to distribute broadband grants depending on how the process unfolds.

The National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) decided last year that states must agree not to enforce any rate regulation or net neutrality rule on ISPs that receive money from the $42 billion Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment (BEAD) program. California had to decide whether to accept its share of the fund despite that restriction. California is slated to spend $1.42 billion to deploy broadband to 270,571 locations, and may ultimately receive up to $1.86 billion from BEAD for a mix of deployment and non-deployment projects.

State officials argue that California should be able to obtain the money and keep enforcing its laws because the Trump administration’s demand would violate the state’s constitutional rights. The California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) made its view clear in a carefully worded letter yesterday to Assistant Secretary of Commerce and NTIA Administrator Arielle Roth.

“The CPUC cannot be bound by any terms or conditions that are unconstitutional or not authorized by law and it expressly does not waive or concede any arguments or challenges concerning the legality, interpretation, or applicability of any term or condition,” CPUC President John Reynolds told Roth.

Reynolds’ letter also said the CPUC cannot prevent other California agencies from enforcing state laws, suggesting that the attorney general would maintain the right to punish misbehaving Internet providers.

Reynolds’ letter acknowledged that the NTIA may not agree with the CPUC’s stance and said the state thus will not distribute any funding to ISPs until after the state and federal agency sort out any differences. If the NTIA refuses to change its position, California could sue the Trump administration on the grounds that the condition is unconstitutional.

The NTIA does not appear likely to bend. “As noted in the Department’s response to CPUC, the terms and conditions of the award constitute the entire agreement between NTIA and CPUC. No part of the letter outlining CPUC’s concerns is incorporated into or made part of the award,” an NTIA spokesperson told Ars today.

Consumer advocacy group Public Knowledge supported CPUC’s position. The Trump administration’s demand to preempt state laws is “brazen and meritless,” the group said.

“This administration’s preposterous demand that industry be given a blanket waiver from affordability requirements, net neutrality and privacy protections, and any other commitments to connect and serve Americans has no basis in the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA), which established BEAD. And, as the commission points out, the NTIA has no authority to alter California state law or require California agencies to not enforce the law,” said Raza Panjwani, senior policy counsel at Public Knowledge.

The CPUC voted to ratify the funding plan in September. But Reynolds said in yesterday’s letter to the Trump administration that his agency’s acceptance of the funds is “based on the CPUC’s best understanding of the effect of Section 50” of the BEAD terms and conditions. Section 50 of the BEAD rules says each state:

shall commit that it will not enforce any law, regulation, order, contracting requirement, or other enforceable obligation that directly or indirectly regulates the rates, terms, and conditions of broadband Internet service… or imposes net neutrality rules, open access, or other utility-style rules on broadband Internet service, against a Subgrantee or its affiliates anywhere it provides service within the State (i.e., both BEAD and non-BEAD locations), while that Subgrantee has any subgrant that is still within its period of performance, extended period of performance, or federal interest period.

The BEAD rules specify that a net neutrality rule is one prohibiting ISPs from “blocking content, throttling speeds, imposing data caps, or engaging in paid prioritization.” ISPs obtaining BEAD funding could be exempt from such laws for up to 14 years.

Reynolds’ letter said the NTIA-imposed condition is “vague and ambiguous as to its scope and its relationship to Section 47 U.S.C. § 1702(g)(2)(A)(i) of the BEAD statute,” the US law that created the BEAD program. He wrote:

The CPUC does not interpret Section 50 to require the CPUC to waive, release, or otherwise forfeit any rights, claims, arguments, or defenses concerning potential implications of Section 50 that may violate applicable laws. Further, the CPUC’s acceptance of funds under this award should not be understood as agreement either to refrain from compliance with mandatory legal duties or obligations, or to constrain other State of California entities in the exercise of their authorities to enforce state law, which is outside the scope of the CPUC’s authority. Moreover, California’s net neutrality law expressly provides that “any waiver of the provisions of this title is contrary to public policy and shall be unenforceable and void.” Likewise, many of the CPUC’s own programs that touch on broadband Internet access service are mandated by the California Public Utilities Code, and are neither discretionary nor waivable.

news.article_content_zh:
尽管拒绝特朗普的行政条件，该州仍试图获得宽带资金。

加州正在接受特朗普政府提供的 14.2 亿美元宽带拨款资金，但该州没有接受特朗普政府要求其停止执行网络中立法和其他电信法规的要求。

加州反对特朗普政府的立场可能会导致涉及州、联邦政府和寻求政府资金的互联网提供商的多起法律诉讼。尽管加州告诉联邦政府它将接受这笔钱，但它保留质疑美国施加的条件的权利。该州可能会推迟或取消分配宽带拨款的计划，具体取决于进程的进展情况。

美国国家电信和信息管理局 (NTIA) 去年决定，各州必须同意不对从 420 亿美元宽带公平、接入和部署 (BEAD) 计划中获得资金的 ISP 实施任何费率监管或网络中立规则。尽管存在这一限制，加州仍必须决定是否接受其在该基金中的份额。加州计划斥资 14.2 亿美元在 270,571 个地点部署宽带，最终可能从 BEAD 获得高达 18.6 亿美元的部署和非部署项目。

州官员认为，加州应该能够获得这笔资金并继续执行其法律，因为特朗普政府的要求将侵犯该州的宪法权利。加州公用事业委员会 (CPUC) 昨天在致助理商务部长兼 NTIA 局长 Arielle Roth 的一封措辞谨慎的信中明确表达了自己的观点。

“CPUC 不受任何违宪或未经法律授权的条款或条件的约束，并且明确不会放弃或承认任何有关任何条款或条件的合法性、解释或适用性的争论或质疑，”CPUC 主席约翰·雷诺兹 (John Reynolds) 告诉罗斯。

雷诺兹的信中还表示，CPUC 无法阻止加州其他机构执行州法律，这表明总检察长将保留惩罚行为不当的互联网提供商的权利。

雷诺兹在信中承认 NTIA 可能不同意 CPUC 的立场，并表示在州和联邦机构解决任何分歧之前，州不会向 ISP 分配任何资金。如果 NTIA 拒绝改变立场，加州可能会以该条件违宪为由起诉特朗普政府。

NTIA 似乎不太可能弯曲。 NTIA 发言人今天告诉 Ars：“正如该部门对 CPUC 的回应中所指出的，该裁决的条款和条件构成了 NTIA 与 CPUC 之间的完整协议。信中概述 CPUC 担忧的任何部分均未纳入该裁决或成为该裁决的一部分。”

消费者权益倡导组织 Public Knowledge 支持 CPUC 的立场。该组织表示，特朗普政府要求优先于各州法律的要求是“厚颜无耻且毫无根据的”。

Public Knowledge 高级政策顾问 Raza Panjwani 表示：“本届政府荒谬地要求行业全面豁免承受能力要求、网络中立性和隐私保护以及任何其他连接和服务美国人的承诺，这在建立 BEAD 的基础设施投资和就业法案 (IIJA) 中没有任何依据。而且，正如委员会指出的那样，NTIA 无权改变加州法律或要求加州机构不执行法律。”

CPUC 于 9 月投票批准了该资助计划。但雷诺兹在昨天给特朗普政府的信中表示，他的机构接受这笔资金是“基于 CPUC 对 BEAD 条款和条件第 50 条影响的最佳理解”。 BEAD 规则第 50 条规定，每个州：

应承诺，当子受让人拥有仍处于其履行期限、延长期限内的任何分赠款时，不会对子受让人或其在州内提供服务的任何地方（即 BEAD 和非 BEAD 地点）的附属机构执行任何直接或间接规范宽带互联网服务的费率、条款和条件的法律、法规、命令、合同要求或其他可执行义务……或对宽带互联网服务强加网络中立规则、开放接入或其他公用事业风格的规则。绩效或联邦利息期。

BEAD 规则规定，网络中立性规则是禁止 ISP“阻止内容、限制速度、施加数据上限或参与付费优先级”的规则。获得 BEAD 资助的 ISP 可以在长达 14 年的时间内免受此类法律的约束。

news.title: Following backlash against its education updates, Google says schools can choose to enable Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search individually (Isabel O'Brien/CNBC)
news.title_en: Following backlash against its education updates, Google says schools can choose to enable Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search individually (Isabel O'Brien/CNBC)
news.author: CNBC
news.article_content:
Google is playing defense on Tuesday after a political backlash to its new policy surrounding use of artificial intelligence in schools.

In a blog post titled "Designing responsible AI for learning," Google said it's bringing AI into its Classroom offering with a product called Guided Learning. The New York Times published a story saying that the company will turn off search for schools that reject AI entirely.

Following the Times' story, prominent left-leaning politicians, including Sen. Bernie Sanders from Vermont and New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani voiced their outrage on social media.

"Google is trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools," Mamdani wrote on X. Sanders wrote that "Google is threatening schools," referring to the policy as "extortion."

Google responded later in the day. In a post on X, the company said its new policy was meant to give schools more choice over how students interact with AI. Google said its Gemini chatbot, Gemini Notebook and search are turned off by default, and that "schools are in control," with the ability to turn them as they see fit.

"We are also updating Search for schools to make it better for learning," Google wrote. "Specifically, AI Mode and AI Overviews will offer step-by-step guided learning through problems, so that students don't get quick answers to schoolwork."

The company's post didn't explicitly respond to the claim that access to search requires use of AI. However, Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google, told the Times that "Search and AI are deeply integrated."

A Google spokesperson referred CNBC to the X post when asked for comment.

Google's broader practices have come under fire in recent years, with the company losing antitrust cases over its search and advertising businesses. Former Federal Trade Commission Chair Lina Khan aggressively pursued Google and other tech giants, including Meta and Amazon.

Khan said in a post on X on Tuesday that Google's new AI for learning policy highlights "the danger of allowing an unregulated monopolist to control an essential service."

It's the latest controversy related to the impact of technology on children and the role leading internet companies are playing in delivering information.

In August, Meta reached a landmark $16.7 billion settlement in its child safety trial after a number of state attorneys general accused the company of misrepresenting the extent of child mental health harms caused by apps like Facebook and Instagram.

The same month, OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Teens after state attorneys general launched an investigation into the company's safety practices, with Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier, a Republican, filing a lawsuit in June.

The nonprofit Common Sense Media recently gave Google's AI overviews an "unacceptable risk" rating. Last month, Sens. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., and Josh Hawley, R-Mo., launched an inquiry over Google's push of AI into classrooms.

Google introduced AI overviews as a search function in May 2024.

— CNBC's MacKenzie Sigalos contributed to this report.

WATCH: Meta settled its child safety lawsuit. Now comes the hard part.

news.article_content_zh:
谷歌周二在学校使用人工智能的新政策遭到政治强烈反对后，采取了防御措施。

谷歌在一篇题为“为学习设计负责任的人工智能”的博客文章中表示，它将通过一款名为“引导学习”的产品将人工智能引入其课堂产品。 《纽约时报》发表报道称，该公司将停止搜索完全拒绝人工智能的学校。

在《泰晤士报》报道后，包括佛蒙特州参议员伯尼·桑德斯和纽约市长佐兰·马姆达尼在内的著名左倾政客在社交媒体上表达了他们的愤怒。

Mamdani 在 X 上写道：“谷歌正试图利用其垄断力量迫使人工智能进入我们的公立学校。”桑德斯写道，“谷歌正在威胁学校”，并将该政策称为“勒索”。

谷歌当天晚些时候做出了回应。该公司在 X 上的一篇帖子中表示，其新政策旨在让学校在学生与人工智能互动的方式上有更多选择。谷歌表示，其 Gemini 聊天机器人、Gemini Notebook 和搜索默认情况下处于关闭状态，并且“学校处于控制之中”，可以根据需要关闭它们。

谷歌写道：“我们还在更新学校搜索，以使其更好地学习。” “具体来说，人工智能模式和人工智能概述将通过问题提供逐步指导学习，这样学生就不会快速获得作业的答案。”

该公司的帖子没有明确回应访问搜索需要使用人工智能的说法。然而，谷歌教育副总裁克里斯·菲利普斯(Chris Phillips)告诉《泰晤士报》，“搜索和人工智能是深度融合的。”

当被要求置评时，谷歌发言人向 CNBC 推荐了 X 帖子。

近年来，谷歌更广泛的做法受到了批评，该公司在搜索和广告业务方面输掉了反垄断诉讼。前联邦贸易委员会主席莉娜·汗 (Lina Khan) 积极追捧谷歌和其他科技巨头，包括 Meta 和亚马逊。

Khan 周二在 X 上发帖称，谷歌新的人工智能学习政策凸显了“允许不受监管的垄断者控制基本服务的危险”。

这是有关技术对儿童的影响以及领先的互联网公司在传递信息方面所扮演的角色的最新争议。

8 月，Meta 在儿童安全审判中达成了具有里程碑意义的 167 亿美元和解协议，此前一些州总检察长指控该公司歪曲了 Facebook 和 Instagram 等应用程序对儿童心理健康造成的伤害程度。

同月，在各州总检察长对该公司的安全实践发起调查后，OpenAI 推出了针对青少年的 ChatGPT，佛罗里达州总检察长、共和党人 James Uthmeier 于 6 月提起诉讼。

非营利组织 Common Sense Media 最近给予谷歌的人工智能概述“不可接受的风险”评级。上个月，康涅狄格州民主党参议员理查德·布卢门撒尔 (Richard Blumenthal) 和密苏里州共和党参议员乔什·霍利 (Josh Hawley) 对谷歌将人工智能推入课堂的行为发起了调查。

news.title: Cat Wu, product lead for Claude Code and Cowork, has left Anthropic; Thariq Shihipar, who worked on Claude Code, announced his departure last month (Stephen Council/Business Insider)
news.title_en: Cat Wu, product lead for Claude Code and Cowork, has left Anthropic; Thariq Shihipar, who worked on Claude Code, announced his departure last month (Stephen Council/Business Insider)
news.author: Business Insider
news.article_content:
Cat Wu, a top product manager at Anthropic and one of a small group behind the launch of its blockbuster tool Claude Code, left the company on Friday. Wu announced her departure on Tuesday afternoon on X, thanking the Claude Code team and its users and reflecting on the tool's progress.

As the head of product for Claude Code, Wu served as one of the two top leaders and evangelists for the technology alongside its original creator, Boris Cherny. Claude Code, under Wu and Cherny's leadership, turned into one of the most important products in the AI industry's history.

The tech gave Anthropic the viral product it needed to boost its revenues and access more funding for compute, and it turned the company into a bigger rival for OpenAI. Wu did not say what prompted her departure and did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

She's leaving at a crucial moment for Anthropic, as it churns toward a gargantuan initial public offering later this month. The company confirmed her departure.

Thariq Shihipar, who also worked on Claude Code, announced his own departure last month. Wu joined Anthropic in summer 2024 and tested an early prototype of Claude Code.

In Tuesday's post, she reminisced on that moment: "It worked, I was hooked, and I joined the team." Anthropic released the tool in research preview in February 2025, announcing it in a brief demo video that featured Wu and Cherny.

The two decamped to AI coding startup Cursor that summer, and then returned to Anthropic a couple of weeks later, The Information reported. Wu and Cherny then oversaw Claude Code's meteoric rise, which ramped up at the end of 2025.

The tool first grew popular as an automatic coder for software engineers, who suddenly had a product that could sprint through entire coding tasks. Tech giants' AI bills with Anthropic soared as more developers started burning through Claude tokens.

Wu also oversees Cowork, Anthropic's tool for non-coding work, which relies on the same AI models and handles knowledge work for non-software engineers. In an interview on Lenny's Podcast in April, Wu described her role as figuring out the path to bring Claude Code to the "AGI-pilled" version that Cherny envisioned for the future — a reference to the industry term "artificial general intelligence." In her role, Wu said she worked with marketing, sales, finance, and other teams, and hired some of Anthropic's product managers.

She also regularly responded to user requests about Claude Code on social media. One commenter wrote under her X post on Tuesday, "Are you gonna take that 6 months vacations now?" Wu answered: "post agi!"

news.article_content_zh:
Anthropic 核心产品负责人、主导推出重磅大模型编码工具 Claude Code 的核心骨干之一 Cat Wu 已于上周五正式离职。Wu 于周二下午在社交平台 X 上公开宣布了这一消息，向 Claude Code 团队及其全球开发者致谢，并回顾了该工具一路走来的突破历程。

作为 Claude Code 的产品总负责人，Wu 与该工具的最初缔造者 Boris Cherny 并肩作战，共同担任该技术的核心领袖与布道者。在 Wu 和 Cherny 的带领下，Claude Code 迅速发展成为人工智能产业史上最具里程碑意义的产品之一。

这项技术不仅为 Anthropic 提供了引爆全网的杀手级应用，推动其营收实现指数级跃升并获取更多算力资金支持，更使 Anthropic 成为足以正面撼动 OpenAI 统治地位的头号竞争对手。Wu 尚未对外透露离职具体动因，也未立即回应媒体的置评请求。

她的离开恰逢 Anthropic 发展的关键十字路口——公司正全力冲刺本月晚些时候估值高达数千亿美元的重磅 IPO 上市。Anthropic 官方已向媒体正式确认了她的离职。而同在 Claude Code 核心团队担任关键角色的 Thariq Shihipar 也已在上月宣布离开。

Wu 于 2024 年夏天加入 Anthropic，并深度参与了 Claude Code 最早期原型的测试。在周二的告别长文中，她深情回忆道：“当时它跑通了，我彻底被震撼并深陷其中，于是毫不犹豫加入了这个团队。” 随后，Anthropic 于 2025 年 2 月正式推出该工具的研究预览版，并在由 Wu 与 Cherny 联袂出镜的简短演示视频中向全球发布。

据 The Information 披露，两人曾在那年夏天短暂跳槽至新兴 AI 编程初创公司 Cursor，但几周后便迅速重返 Anthropic。随后，Wu 与 Cherny 亲历并主导了 Claude Code 在 2025 年底的爆发式增长。该工具最初作为软件工程师的“自动代码生成神兵”迅速风靡全球开发者社区，使程序员首次拥有了能够自主冲刺、端到端攻克整套编码任务的生产级工具。随着大批开发者日夜消耗海量 Claude Token，各大科技巨头支付给 Anthropic 的 AI 算力账单呈爆炸式激增。

除了 Claude Code，Wu 还负责掌管 Anthropic 专为非技术人员打造的工作流协作工具 Cowork，该工具基于相同的底层基础大模型，赋能非工程师群体高效处理高复杂度知识工作。在 4 月份接受知名科技播客 Lenny's Podcast 专访时，Wu 将自己的核心使命概括为：铺就一条切实可行的工程路径，将 Claude Code 推向 Cherny 所构想的终极“AGI 强化形态（AGI-pilled）”——直指通用人工智能的技术远景。她表示自己在岗位上统筹协调市场、销售、财务及跨部门资源，招募了多位核心产品经理，并长期在社交媒体一线直接响应全球开发者对 Claude Code 的产品迭代诉求。

周二，一位社区评论者在她的 X 离职帖下半开玩笑地留言道：“那你现在打算去休 6 个月的长假吗？” Wu 随即可爱而坚定地回复道：“等实现了通用人工智能（AGI）之后再说吧！”

news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
People, including on this staff, keep asking me with varying degrees of excitement or trepidation when the AI bubble will burst. I'll tell you what I tell them: If I knew that, I would make a life-changing bet on the market, levered up as far as I could, and then, after I made my money, go retire on a beach somewhere. Maybe run a cat sanctuary, who knows.

news.summary_en: A prominent tech editor addressed the relentless public obsession with the impending AI bubble, prompted by Wall Street CEOs clashing over AI risks at the Global Financial Leaders' Investment Summit in Hong Kong. The author candidly admitted that if anyone actually knew when the bubble would burst, they would heavily leverage the market for a life-changing retirement rather than writing articles. This ongoing debate highlights the financial sector's collective anxiety of chasing massive AI gains while desperately trying not to be left holding the bag.

news.title: Valve announces changes to Steam's review process, as a surge in game submissions pushes review times to "up to 12 business days", instead of the usual 3-5 days (Jay Peters/The Verge)
news.title_en: Valve announces changes to Steam's review process, as a surge in game submissions pushes review times to "up to 12 business days", instead of the usual 3-5 days (Jay Peters/The Verge)
news.author: The Verge
news.article_content:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Valve admits that it’s now taking ‘up to 12 business days’ to review games.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

In a new post today, Valve acknowledged that it’s seen “a significant increase in submissions for store and page review in recent months” and says it’s “running a little behind” by taking “up to 12 business days” for reviews instead of the typical 3-5 days.

Indie developers have recently expressed frustrations over lengthy approval times for Steam games, even causing some games to miss planned launch dates. Valve says that “much” of the delay is having to re-review games, so it’s making some changes to the release checklist for developers to hopefully “cut down on re-reviews for basic functional issues.”

The changes include requiring developers to run games through Steam for at least five minutes. “Believe it or not, sometimes we review builds that have not ever been played through Steam,” Valve says. “This means that even if a game runs smoothly when a dev launches their executable directly, they might have missed basic steps that would impact a user installing and playing via Steam.”

Other requirements include making sure that achievements are ready and confirming any required common redistributables, like DirectX or Visual C++, that Steam may need to install.

Valve also says more improvements are in the works for the build review process.

news.summary_zh: 由于开发者提交数量暴增，Steam审核周期延长至12个工作日，官方正通过强制测试要求来优化流程
news.article_content_zh:
该主题的帖子将添加到您的每日电子邮件摘要和主页源中。

Valve 承认现在需要“最多 12 个工作日”来审核游戏。

该作者的帖子将添加到您的每日电子邮件摘要和主页源中。

在今天的一篇新帖子中，Valve 承认“近几个月来提交的商店和页面审核数量显着增加”，并表示“有点落后”，审核需要“最多 12 个工作日”，而不是通常的 3-5 天。

独立开发者最近对 Steam 游戏审批时间过长表示不满，甚至导致一些游戏错过了计划的发布日期。 Valve 表示，延迟的“大部分”是因为必须重新审查游戏，因此它正在对开发者的发行清单进行一些更改，以期“减少对基本功能问题的重新审查”。

这些变化包括要求开发者通过 Steam 运行游戏至少五分钟。 “不管你信不信，有时我们会审查那些从未在 Steam 上玩过的版本，”Valve 说道。 “这意味着，即使开发者直接启动可执行文件时游戏运行顺利，他们也可能错过了影响用户通过 Steam 安装和玩游戏的基本步骤。”

其他要求包括确保成就已准备就绪，并确认 Steam 可能需要安装的任何必需的常见可再发行组件，例如 DirectX 或 Visual C++。

Valve 还表示，构建审核流程的更多改进正在进行中。

news.author: The Age
news.article_content:

Canva will cut more than 1000 jobs in a major restructure in response to slowing growth at the design giant.

Co-founder and chief executive Melanie Perkins told staff on Wednesday the Sydney design company needed to “refound Canva” and return to small, empowered teams after its growth slowed this year for the first time in a decade. The shake-up will affect 1271 jobs, or 22 per cent of its workforce, with some staff to lose their roles and others asked to relocate to centralised hubs.

Canva co-founders Cliff Obrecht, Melanie Perkins and Cameron Adams.Bloomberg“This is without doubt the hardest moment in our thirteen-year history,” she wrote.

“After exploring a wide range of alternatives, I’ve come to the difficult conclusion that small changes won’t be enough. To set ourselves up for the next decade, we need to refound Canva, getting back to our roots of small, empowered teams with the freedom to make decisions, take ownership, and focus on what matters most for our community.”

Canva will merge its product, growth and platform teams into a single product organisation and cut management layers. Sydney will become the primary home for more product teams, and hybrid staff will be expected in the office two to three days a week from January.

The shake-up comes as investor fears that AI will undercut software businesses have hammered design companies. Shares in rival Figma more than halved in 2026 to the end of April, despite strong revenue growth.

Blackbird, Canva’s biggest venture backer, cut its valuation of the company by 17 per cent to $US34.9 billion in August, with Airtree making the same cut from the $US42 billion set in a 2025 employee share sale. Canva’s own internal valuation fell to $US31 billion, this masthead revealed in August.

Departing staff will receive at least six months’ salary, 12 months of healthcare where Canva provides it, and can keep their work MacBooks. They can also apply for $US10,000 ($14,500) grants to start their own ventures.

Canva 将在重大重组中裁员 1000 多人，以应对这家设计巨头增长放缓的情况。

联合创始人兼首席执行官 Melanie Perkins 周三告诉员工，这家悉尼设计公司在今年增长十年来首次放缓后，需要“重新组建 Canva”并回归小型、授权的团队。此次人事变动将影响 1271 个工作岗位，占员工总数的 22%，部分员工将失去职位，其他员工则被要求搬迁到集中中心。

Canva 联合创始人 Cliff Obrecht、Melanie Perkins 和 Cameron Adams。彭博社“这无疑是我们十三年历史上最艰难的时刻，”她写道。

“在探索了广泛的替代方案之后，我得出了一个艰难的结论：小小的改变是不够的。为了为下一个十年做好准备，我们需要重新建立 Canva，回到我们的小而授权团队的根源，让他们可以自由地做出决策、掌握所有权并专注于对我们社区最重要的事情。”

Canva 将把其产品、增长和平台团队合并为一个产品组织，并削减管理层。悉尼将成为更多产品团队的主要所在地，从一月份开始，混合型员工预计每周在办公室工作两到三天。

此次重组发生之际，投资者担心人工智能将削弱软件业务，这给设计公司带来了沉重打击。尽管收入增长强劲，但截至 2026 年 4 月底，竞争对手 Figma 的股价将减少一半以上。

Canva 最大的风险投资公司 Blackbird 在 8 月份将该公司的估值下调了 17%，至 349 亿美元，Airtree 在 2025 年员工股票出售中设定的 420 亿美元也进行了同样的削减。该报头在 8 月份透露，Canva 的内部估值已降至 310 亿美元。

离职员工将获得至少六个月的工资、Canva 提供的 12 个月的医疗保健，并且可以保留他们的工作 MacBook。他们还可以申请 10,000 美元（14,500 美元）的补助金来创办自己的企业。

news.title: Revolut says it cut AI coding inference costs by ~90% in less than a year by making self-hosted GLM models its default over commercial tools like Claude Code (Tobias Mann/The Register)
news.title_en: Revolut says it cut AI coding inference costs by ~90% in less than a year by making self-hosted GLM models its default over commercial tools like Claude Code (Tobias Mann/The Register)
news.author: The Register
news.article_content:
Tobias Mann Tobias Mann SYSTEMS EDITOR Published tue 3 Nov 2026 // 20:07 UTC Make us preferred on Google READ MORE Nvidia is happy to take your money whether you're using open or closed models, says Jensen Huang 17 minutes ago Drax wants to feed Britain's AI habit with £20B datacenter at biomass power station 7 hours ago Toyota shows off SoC that stores model weights and its OS on integrated memory 17 hours ago Anthropic's compute tab could top $1T as Q3 revenue nears $17B 21 hours ago Marvell wants to be a copper topper, bets $115B on photonics leader to push optical networking 1 day ago Revolut says that in less than a year it's managed to slash its AI coding inference costs by roughly 90 percent by making self-hosted models its default instead of relying primarily on commercial services like Claude.

Speaking at the AI Engineer conference in New York last month, David Abitbol, ops and infrastructure lead at the British fintech, described how it saw a 60 percent improvement in coding time and a 70 percent improvement in lead time following its rollout of AI coding tools to roughly 2,000 engineers. Revolut initially adopted GLM-5.1 before moving to GLM-5.3, which it now serves using 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs.

Prior to its switch to GLM, Revolut had been experimenting with AI, deploying Gemini in early 2025 and Claude Code in early 2026. "We were highly skeptical about the cost of AI. We were seeing engineers spend $1,000 a month, $10,000 a month with not so much ROI, and so when we launched it we launched it with strict budget limits," Abitbol said.

Because of this, engineers only had access to a limited number of tokens, so the company began investigating self-hosting iyd own models. At $0.30 per million input/output tokens, self hosting GLM 5.1 cost about a tenth of using OpenAI's Codex or Anthropic's Claude Code. And, as it turned out, when tokens are cheap, you stop worrying about how many they use or what they use them for.

While Revolut did see improvements to coding speed, Abitbol noted the biggest bottleneck wasn't actually the code. Instead, he says the biggest gains came from letting the AI models deal with things like debugging and Jira and Confluence tickets. "When you have unlimited tokens, you're free to do that," he said. "You no longer have to save your tokens for the end of the quarter or the most difficult task."

Developed by Chinese open weights model dev Z.ai, GLM 5.1 isn't exactly a small model. At roughly 754 billion total parameters (40 billion activated for each token generated), the model requires roughly 380 GB of GPU memory just to hold the weights and another 6-26 GB per user to maintain context depending on precision.

To serve GLM-5.3 at scale, Revolut deployed 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs, equivalent in GPU count to seven eight-GPU DGX B200 systems. But as Abitbol noted, the greatest performance gains didn't come from adding GPUs, but rather tuning the model's hyperparameters along with switching to NVFP4 quantization, implementing disaggregated prefill and decode, and tuning context lengths.

One key takeaway was that supporting a one-million-token context window doesn't necessarily make such a large window useful or efficient. "Long context is a scam. You really need to be mindful of that," Abitbol said. "Even though you can serve one million tokens, 256 [thousand] is really what you need."

With these optimizations, Abitbol says that the company was able to achieve sub 3-second time to first token on context windows of around 256,000 tokens, and generation speeds of around 200 tokens a second, both of which he notes are the sweet spot for the company's software engineers.

"What you want to aim for is a sub-3 second time to first token. This is empirical evidence. As soon as you exceed 5 seconds, my Slack inbox starts to blow up," Abitbol said. "In terms of throughput, it doesn't really matter as much. We serve, in terms of interactivity, 200 tokens per second. People are fine [with that]. You don't need to go higher. The way people work has changed. We no longer look at the stream of thinking tokens. People run tasks in parallel and check in when the task is done."

And if throughput is a concern, he notes engineers who sign in after 5 pm are getting closer to 800 tokens a second.

However, it's worth noting that GLM hasn't replaced GPT or Claude entirely. The Chinese model is text only, so it isn't ideal for things like UI work. So instead, Revolut used a model router to direct vision queries to models like Gemini or GPT Luna while keeping code generation running on GLM.

"Open source is now a priority at Revolut, and our economics are favorable. The billing is flat, we don't have any bill shock at the end of the month, and the frontier is the exception," Abitbol said.

Having said that, Abitbol acknowledges that Chinese open weights models may be a concern for privacy and security reasons, but emphasizes that the major concern there is accessing them via APIs running out of China. When run on-prem or on regional cloud resources, there's really nothing to worry about. ®

news.article_content_zh:
Tobias Mann Tobias Mann 系统编辑 发布于 2026 年 11 月 3 日星期二// 20:07 UTC 让我们在 Google 上成为首选 阅读更多 黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 表示，无论您使用的是开放式模型还是封闭式模型，Nvidia 都很乐意接受您的钱 17 分钟前 Drax 希望在生物质发电站利用价值 20B 英镑的数据中心满足英国的人工智能习惯 7 小时前 丰田展示了将模型权重及其操作系统存储在集成内存中的 SoC 17 小时前 Anthropic 的计算选项卡可能会突破 1T 美元，因为第三季度收入接近 17B 美元 21 小时前 Marvell 希望成为铜领先者，在光子学领导者上押注 115B 美元以推动光网络 1 天前 Revolut 表示，在不到一年的时间里，通过将自托管模型设置为默认值，而不是主要依赖 Claude 等商业服务，它已成功将其 AI 编码推理成本削减了约 90%。

上个月在纽约举行的人工智能工程师会议上，英国金融科技公司运营和基础设施负责人 David Abitbol 描述了在向大约 2,000 名工程师推出人工智能编码工具后，编码时间缩短了 60%，交付周期缩短了 70%。 Revolut 最初采用 GLM-5.1，然后转向 GLM-5.3，现在使用 56 个 Nvidia B200 GPU 提供服务。

在转向 GLM 之前，Revolut 一直在尝试人工智能，于 2025 年初部署 Gemini，并于 2026 年初部署 Claude Code。“我们对人工智能的成本非常怀疑。我们看到工程师每月花费 1,000 美元，每月花费 10,000 美元，投资回报率并不高，因此当我们推出它时，我们在严格的预算限制下推出了它，”Abitbol 说。

因此，工程师只能访问有限数量的代币，因此该公司开始研究自托管 iyd 自己的模型。以每百万输入/输出代币 0.30 美元计算，自托管 GLM 5.1 的成本约为使用 OpenAI 的 Codex 或 Anthropic 的 Claude Code 的十分之一。而且，事实证明，当代币便宜时，你就不再担心它们使用了多少或它们用于什么目的。

虽然 Revolut 确实看到了编码速度的提高，但 Abitbol 指出最大的瓶颈实际上并不是代码。相反，他表示最大的收益来自于让人工智能模型处理诸如调试、Jira 和 Confluence 票证之类的事情。 “当你拥有无限的代币时，你就可以自由地这样做，”他说。 “你不再需要为季度末或最困难的任务保存代币。”

GLM 5.1 由中国开放权重模型开发者 Z.ai 开发，并不是一个小模型。该模型总共大约有 7540 亿个参数（每个生成的令牌激活 400 亿个参数），仅需要大约 380 GB 的 GPU 内存来保存权重，每个用户还需要 6-26 GB 的内存来根据精度维护上下文。

为了大规模服务 GLM-5.3，Revolut 部署了 56 个 Nvidia B200 GPU，其 GPU 数量相当于七个 8 个 GPU DGX B200 系统。但正如 Abitbol 指出的那样，最大的性能提升并不是来自添加 GPU，而是调整模型的超参数以及切换到 NVFP4 量化、实现分解的预填充和解码以及调整上下文长度。

一个关键要点是，支持一百万个令牌上下文窗口并不一定会使如此大的窗口有用或高效。 “长上下文是一个骗局。你真的需要注意这一点，”阿比特博尔说。 “尽管你可以提供 100 万个代币，但 256 [千] 个才是你真正需要的。”

Abitbol 表示，通过这些优化，该公司能够在大约 256,000 个代币的上下文窗口上实现不到 3 秒的时间生成第一个代币，并以每秒约 200 个代币的生成速度实现，他指出这两者都是公司软件工程师的最佳选择。

“你想要的目标是在 3 秒内获得第一个令牌。这是经验证据。一旦超过 5 秒，我的 Slack 收件箱就会开始爆炸，”Abitbol 说。 “就吞吐量而言，这并不那么重要。就交互性而言，我们每秒提供 200 个令牌。人们对此很满意。你不需要更高。人们的工作方式已经改变。我们不再关注思考令牌流。人们并行运行任务，并在任务完成时检查。”

如果吞吐量是一个问题，他指出下午 5 点后登录的工程师每秒接近 800 个代币。

然而，值得注意的是，GLM 并没有完全取代 GPT 或 Claude。中文模型仅包含文本，因此对于 UI 工作等内容并不理想。因此，Revolut 使用模型路由器将视觉查询定向到 Gemini 或 GPT Luna 等模型，同时保持代码生成在 GLM 上运行。

Abitbol 表示：“开源现在是 Revolut 的首要任务，而且我们的经济状况良好。账单持平，月底我们没有任何账单冲击，而前沿是个例外。”

话虽如此，Abitbol 承认中国的开放权重模型可能出于隐私和安全原因而令人担忧，但强调主要的担忧是通过中国以外的 API 访问它们。当在本地或区域云资源上运行时，实际上没有什么可担心的。 ®

news.title: Super Micro reports Q1 revenue up 298% YoY to $19.95B, vs. $16.39B est., and forecasts Q2 revenue above estimates; SMCI jumps 7%+ after hours (Reuters)

news.author: Reuters
news.content_snippet: Super Micro Computer (SMCI.O) forecast second-quarter revenue above Wall Street estimates on Tuesday as strong demand for its AI-optimized servers boosted sales …
news.summary_en: Super Micro Computer reported Q1 revenue surging 298% year-over-year to $19.9.5 billion, beating Wall Street's $16.39 billion estimate, driven by explosive AI server demand. The company also issued a stronger-than-expected Q2 revenue forecast, sending its stock up over 7% in after-hours trading.

news.title: AMD reports Q3 revenue up 45% YoY to $13.38B, vs. $13.09B est., Data Center revenue up 97% to $8.5B, forecasts Q4 revenue above est.; AMD jumps 7%+ after hours (Katie Tarasov/CNBC)
news.title_en: AMD reports Q3 revenue up 45% YoY to $13.38B, vs. $13.09B est., Data Center revenue up 97% to $8.5B, forecasts Q4 revenue above est.; AMD jumps 7%+ after hours (Katie Tarasov/CNBC)
news.author: CNBC
news.article_content:
Advanced Micro Devices reported third-quarter earnings on Tuesday that beat Wall Street's expectations, with revenue jump 45% and data center sales nearly doubling from a year earlier. The stock jumped 7% in extended trading.

Revenue increased from $9.25 billion a year earlier, AMD said in a statement.

CEO Lisa Su said in a press release that she expects growth in data center processors to "accelerate further," and that meeting demand won't be a problem.

"With our leadership product portfolio and deep customer and supply chain relationships, we are confident in our ability to sustain very strong revenue growth and expanding profitability over the coming years " Su said in a statement.

AMD's report comes days after Intel disclosed similar data center growth, with revenue in that segment up 78% in the third quarter. But the stock plummeted 29% on Friday over concerns about weak guidance and Intel's ability to meet demand.

The data center unit makes up the majority of AMD's business, accounting for 64% of overall revenue, up from 47% a year ago.

After years spent chasing Nvidia in the market for artificial intelligence graphics processing units, or GPUs, AMD's central processing units, or CPUs, are experiencing a major resurgence with the rise of agentic AI apps like Meta's Muse. AMD's server CPUs are key for agentic apps because they power virtual machines and can run for hours on their own. Demand from agentic AI boosted AMD shares to a record in October.

AMD's stock is up about 125% this year, but it saw three consecutive days of losses before rallying on Tuesday amid an industrywide sell-off tied to fears about overspending on AI.

AMD is also a major player the in weakening PC market, which Intel blamed for its poor outlook last week. AMD and Intel are the largest makers of traditional x86 processors that power many laptops and desktops, while other laptops rely on Arm-based processors from the likes of Qualcomm and Apple.

Global PC shipments declined 4% in the second quarter from a year earlier due to soaring costs for memory and other components, according to Counterpoint Research.

AMD reports PC chip sales in a segment combined with gaming chips. Revenue in that business fell 8% from a year earlier to $3.7 billion. Gaming revenue was down 40% from a year ago.

For the fourth quarter, AMD said it expects about $17 billion in revenue, beating the $16.2 billion average analyst estimate, according to LSEG. AMD sees its gross margin for the quarter coming in at 55%, slightly below the average estimate of 55.3%, according to StreetAccount.

AMD also sells data center GPUs and full rack-scale systems called Helios that compete directly with Nvidia's Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin. Meta, Microsoft, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Oracle are all beginning to use AMD Helios in their data centers. Meta said last week that its Helios racks are up and running, and AMD agreed to invest $1 billion in Meta's equity offering.

AMD has also committed to investing up to $5 billion in Anthropic, which unveiled its highly anticipated prospectus last week as it inches closer to a potentially historic initial public offering.

During a visit to Taiwan in October, Su said she plans to "substantially increase our supply in 2027." Su and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang have both made multiple trips to Taiwan and South Korea this year, holding meetings with key suppliers like Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and memory leaders SK Hynix and Samsung.

In September, AMD said it would acquire World Labs for $8.2 billion in an all-stock deal. The San Francisco-based AI lab, founded by industry pioneer Fei-Fei Li, is developing a so-called world model that simulates 3D environments to aid in developing robots and other physically grounded AI applications.

news.summary_zh: Advanced Micro Devices 周二公布的第三季度财报超出了华尔街的预期，收入增长 45%，数据中心销售额同比增长近一倍。该股在盘后交易中上涨了 7%。 AMD 在一份声明中表示，营收较上年同期的 92.5 亿美元有所增长
news.article_content_zh:
Advanced Micro Devices 周二公布的第三季度财报超出了华尔街的预期，收入增长 45%，数据中心销售额同比增长近一倍。该股在盘后交易中上涨了 7%。

AMD 在一份声明中表示，营收较上年同期的 92.5 亿美元有所增长。

首席执行官苏姿丰(Lisa Su)在一份新闻稿中表示，她预计数据中心处理器的增长将“进一步加速”，满足需求不会成为问题。

苏在一份声明中表示：“凭借我们领先的产品组合以及深厚的客户和供应链关系，我们有信心在未来几年保持强劲的收入增长和不断扩大的盈利能力。”

AMD 发布报告的几天前，英特尔公布了类似的数据中心增长情况，第三季度该领域的收入增长了 78%。但由于对疲弱的指引和英特尔满足需求的能力的担忧，该股周五暴跌 29%。

数据中心部门构成了 AMD 业务的大部分，占总收入的 64%，高于一年前的 47%。

经过多年在人工智能图形处理单元（GPU）市场上追赶 Nvidia 后，随着 Meta 的 Muse 等代理人工智能应用程序的兴起，AMD 的中央处理单元（CPU）正在经历一次重大复苏。 AMD 的服务器 CPU 是代理应用程序的关键，因为它们为虚拟机提供动力，并且可以自行运行数小时。代理人工智能的需求推动 AMD 股价在 10 月份创下历史新高。

AMD 的股价今年上涨了约 125%，但由于担心人工智能超支而引发全行业抛售，该公司股价连续三天下跌，然后在周二反弹。

AMD 也是疲软的个人电脑市场的主要参与者，英特尔上周将其糟糕的前景归咎于 PC 市场。 AMD 和英特尔是传统 x86 处理器的最大制造商，为许多笔记本电脑和台式机提供动力，而其他笔记本电脑则依赖高通和苹果等公司基于 Arm 的处理器。

Counterpoint Research 的数据显示，由于内存和其他组件成本飙升，第二季度全球个人电脑出货量同比下降 4%。

AMD 报告了 PC 芯片与游戏芯片领域的销售额。该业务的收入较上年同期下降 8%，至 37 亿美元。游戏收入同比下降 40%。

据 LSEG 称，AMD 预计第四季度营收约为 170 亿美元，超过分析师平均预期 162 亿美元。据 StreetAccount 称，AMD 预计本季度毛利率为 55%，略低于平均预期 55.3%。

AMD 还销售数据中心 GPU 和名为 Helios 的全机架规模系统，与 Nvidia 的 Grace Blackwell 和 Vera Rubin 直接竞争。 Meta、Microsoft、Anthropic、OpenAI 和 Oracle 都开始在其数据中心使用 AMD Helios。 Meta 上周表示，其 Helios 机架已启动并运行，AMD 同意向 Meta 的股票发行投资 10 亿美元。

AMD 还承诺向 Anthropic 投资高达 50 亿美元，该公司上周公布了备受期待的招股说明书，距离潜在的历史性首次公开募股越来越近。

news.author: Bloomberg
news.content_snippet: Microsoft's gaming unit is looking to divest the French company behind ‘Dishonored’ and 'Marvel's Blade' — Multiple companies have made offers …
news.summary_en: Microsoft's gaming division is seeking to divest the French studio Arkane, with Ubisoft and at least two other companies submitting acquisition offers. The move follows Microsoft's recent efforts to streamline its gaming portfolio after the Activision Blizzard acquisition.

Roy Rinberg (Anthropic), Alex Allain (Anthropic); Alessandro Chiesa (EPFL, StarkWare), Miranda Christ (MIT, RESI), Rahul Dalal (Anthropic STEM Fellows Program, Succinct), Giacomo Fenzi (EPFL), Ben Mayer (Anthropic Fellows Program, MIT), Guy Weissenberg (EPFL)

When you talk to a friend in person, you have many ways to know it is really them: you can see them, hear them, shake their hand. When you talk to an AI model, you have almost none. A user querying a model today cannot check that the responses came from the specific model that a developer claims is responding, as opposed to one secretly substituted in by a routing service for cost reasons, or even by an attacker who has tampered with the token stream. Judging from the model’s output alone is unreliable, even if it produces high-quality responses. Cryptographic proofs of inference solve this problem: they let a model provider commit to a model and then prove that each response was produced by that model. Such proofs could enable applications ranging from consumer products to internal security, and could contribute to a toolkit for verifying compliance with AI pacing requirements.

Specifically, we have made progress on a powerful type of cryptographic proof known as a “zkSNARK”, which is uniquely fit for provable inference (owing to its strong hiding and efficiency properties). In this post, we share some of that progress, primarily through a system we call FlashProve. A brief technical summary is as follows:

We release our code, Lean proofs, and documentation under the Apache 2.0 license.1 This research post is meant to share intermediate progress, and not a completed research agenda. We are sharing this explicitly with the goal that others look at what we have done, take it, and improve it.

When a user sends a request to an AI model, today they have no way of knowing for certain that the model they selected is the one that generated the response. For everyday uses, in which users mostly care about the output and not necessarily which specific model produced it, this is a less pressing concern. But there are several cases where such assurance would be useful. For example, independent evaluators who test AI models before and after release need to know that the model they are evaluating is the model being served. Clients who use a model through a third-party routing service want assurance that the tokens came from the model they paid for. And if a cyberattacker modifies the token stream while pretending to be a given model, a user has no way to detect it from the output alone.

However, enabling verification of model responses is challenging. Most frontier models’ weights are kept private, and even if the user had access to the weights, checking that a given response was produced by a model with those weights would involve running the model, which requires computational resources far beyond what a typical user (or even evaluator) can afford.

The goal of provable inference (PI) is to enable a user with limited computational resources and without any information about the weights to verify that a response came from the requested model. PI is motivated both by a desire to increase customer trust in AI providers, and—because it can be used to provide assurances to independent evaluators and allows providers to demonstrate that they are meeting certain commitments and legal obligations—it also has implications for pacing the frontier of AI development and for AI regulation.

One way to implement PI is via a cryptographic object called a zero-knowledge succinct argument: the model provider sends, along with the claimed response, a short proof (say, a few megabytes) that the user can quickly verify (ideally, in seconds on a CPU). If the claimed response deviates from the specified model, the user’s check will fail. Importantly, cryptographic techniques ensure that the proof reveals nothing about the model’s weights.

Today, we release FlashProve: an open-source performant prototype for provable inference. For a 400B-parameter mixture-of-experts model (Llama 4 Maverick, 4-bit quantization), we show that a single H100 GPU generates proofs at over 100 tokens/second, with proof size of ~19 MB per 1,024-token request (~70-95 times the GPU time that vLLM, a common open-source library, takes to process prompts of the same length).

The release comes with executable code, Lean formalization, and a technical description of the protocol. Our aim is twofold: (i) accelerating and facilitating the development of provable inference; and (ii) demonstrating that zero-knowledge succinct arguments are practical for provable inference.

We believe that this progress has meaningful implications for security, in pacing AI development, in providing AI customers with integrity guarantees, in facilitating tooling for auditors and regulators, and more.

The development of artificial intelligence and its growing role in our digital infrastructure and economy raises trust challenges that AI providers must answer. Addressing these and other challenges is facilitated by relying on tools for provable inference (PI).

Tools for PI include hardware approaches, software approaches, or a combination of both. Here, we focus on a software-only approach: a cryptographic tool known as a “zkSNARK” (zero-knowledge succinct argument of knowledge). Informally, a zkSNARK is a system allowing a prover to convince a verifier, by way of a short “certificate”, that a given computation was executed correctly; crucially, the certificate is zero-knowledge in that it reveals no information beyond what is implied by the computation’s correctness and is succinct in that it’s exponentially faster to verify compared to the proved computation.

Below we outline several challenges and how zkSNARKs help in addressing them.

news.article_content_zh:
罗伊·林伯格（人类）、亚历克斯·阿兰（人类）； Alessandro Chiesa（洛桑联邦理工学院、StarkWare）、Miranda Christ（麻省理工学院、RESI）、Rahul Dalal（人类 STEM 研究员计划，简明）、Giacomo Fenzi（洛桑联邦理工学院）、Ben Mayer（人类研究员计划，麻省理工学院）、Guy Weissenberg（洛桑联邦理工学院）

当您亲自与朋友交谈时，您可以通过多种方式知道那确实是他们：您可以看到他们、听到他们、与他们握手。当你与人工智能模型交谈时，你几乎什么也没有。今天查询模型的用户无法检查响应是否来自开发人员声称正在响应的特定模型，而不是出于成本原因被路由服务秘密替换的模型，甚至是被篡改令牌流的攻击者替换的模型。仅从模型的输出来看是不可靠的，即使它产生了高质量的响应。加密推理证明解决了这个问题：它们让模型提供者提交一个模型，然后证明每个响应都是由该模型生成的。此类证明可以支持从消费产品到内部安全的各种应用，并有助于构建用于验证是否符合人工智能节奏要求的工具包。

具体来说，我们在一种称为“zkSNARK”的强大加密证明方面取得了进展，它特别适合可证明的推理（由于其强大的隐藏性和效率特性）。在这篇文章中，我们主要通过我们称为 FlashProve 的系统分享了其中的一些进展。简要技术总结如下：

我们在 Apache 2.0 许可证下发布我们的代码、精益证明和文档。1 这篇研究文章旨在分享中间进展，而不是完整的研究议程。我们明确分享这一点的目的是让其他人看看我们所做的事情，接受并改进它。

当用户向人工智能模型发送请求时，他们现在无法确定他们选择的模型是否是生成响应的模型。对于日常使用，用户最关心的是输出，而不一定是哪个特定模型产生的，这是一个不太紧迫的问题。但在某些情况下，这种保证是有用的。例如，在发布之前和之后测试人工智能模型的独立评估者需要知道他们正在评估的模型是正在服务的模型。通过第三方路由服务使用模型的客户希望确保代币来自他们支付的模型。如果网络攻击者在冒充给定模型的同时修改了令牌流，则用户无法仅从输出中检测到它。

然而，验证模型响应具有挑战性。大多数前沿模型的权重都是保密的，即使用户可以访问权重，检查给定的响应是否是由具有这些权重的模型生成的也需要运行模型，这需要的计算资源远远超出了典型用户（甚至评估者）可以承受的范围。

可证明推理 (PI) 的目标是使计算资源有限且没有任何权重信息的用户能够验证响应是否来自所请求的模型。 PI 的动机不仅是希望增加客户对人工智能提供商的信任，而且因为它可以用来向独立评估者提供保证，并允许提供商证明他们正在履行某些承诺和法律义务，它还对人工智能开发前沿和人工智能监管产生影响。

实现 PI 的一种方法是通过称为零知识简洁参数的加密对象：模型提供者与声明的响应一起发送一个简短的证明（例如，几兆字节），用户可以快速验证（理想情况下，在 CPU 上只需几秒钟）。如果声称的响应偏离指定模型，则用户的检查将失败。重要的是，加密技术确保证明不会透露任何有关模型权重的信息。

今天，我们发布了 FlashProve：一个用于可证明推理的开源高性能原型。对于 400B 参数混合专家模型（Llama 4 Maverick，4 位量化），我们表明单个 H100 GPU 以超过 100 个令牌/秒的速度生成证明，每个 1,024 个令牌请求的证明大小约为 19 MB（大约是常见开源库 vLLM 处理相同长度提示所需的 GPU 时间的 70-95 倍）。

该版本附带可执行代码、精益形式化和协议的技术描述。我们的目标有两个：（i）加速和促进可证明推理的发展； (ii) 证明零知识简洁论证对于可证明的推理是实用的。

我们相信，这一进展对于安全、加快人工智能开发速度、为人工智能客户提供完整性保证、为审计员和监管机构提供工具等方面具有重要意义。

人工智能的发展及其在数字基础设施和经济中日益增长的作用提出了人工智能提供商必须应对的信任挑战。依靠可证明推理 (PI) 工具可以帮助解决这些和其他挑战。

PI 工具包括硬件方法、软件方法或两者的组合。在这里，我们专注于一种纯软件方法：一种称为“zkSNARK”（零知识简洁知识论证）的加密工具。非正式地说，zkSNARK 是一个系统，允许证明者通过简短的“证书”让验证者相信给定的计算已正确执行；至关重要的是，该证书是零知识的，因为它不会透露超出计算正确性所暗示的信息，而且它很简洁，因为与经过证明的计算相比，它的验证速度要快得多。

下面我们概述了几个挑战以及 zkSNARK 如何帮助解决这些挑战。

news.title: Those Jeff Bezos hair transplant photos are very fake
news.title_en: Those Jeff Bezos hair transplant photos are very fake
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and actor Jason Statham have a distinctive feature in common: They're both famously bald, and that definitely hasn't changed in the last few days. However, there are some images of the two men circulating around X, Threads, and Bluesky in which they both have substantially more hair than their usual shaved look, which in Bezos' case appears to be very freshly transplanted. It's all just photo editing fakery, AI or otherwise.

It's unclear how viral these posts are, but they're prevalent enough that a few members of the Verge team have encountered them in their social media feeds. Some people who shared them claimed  …

news.summary_en: Recent images circulating on social media showing Jeff Bezos and Jason Statham with full heads of hair have sparked speculation. It has been confirmed that these images are fake, created via AI or photo manipulation; neither man has actually changed their hairstyle.

news.article_content_zh:
此次更新不仅是接口层面的开放，更是苹果对iOS交互逻辑的一次彻底重构。通过赋予Siri跨应用调用的能力，苹果试图将AI直接植入到操作系统的毛细血管中，从而在激烈的AI硬件竞争中守住生态壁垒。

开发者被要求配置特定的“技能包”，这意味着未来Siri将不再只是单纯的听指令，而是能够理解用户在屏幕上所见的内容，并主动关联后台服务。这一举措标志着苹果正在试图通过高度整合的AI中台，反向定义移动操作系统的交互范式。

news.title: Apple opens Siri AI to all developers with iOS 27.3 and other 27.3 OS betas, letting any app bring its content and actions into Siri AI by using App Intents (Apple Developer)
news.title_en: Apple opens Siri AI to all developers with iOS 27.3 and other 27.3 OS betas, letting any app bring its content and actions into Siri AI by using App Intents (Apple Developer)
news.author: Apple Developer
news.article_content:
Starting today with the iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, macOS 27.3, and visionOS 27.3 betas, a new Developer Preview enables any developer to integrate their app with Siri AI, giving businesses and developers new ways to reach and serve their customers.

Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri that is profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal, is designed to be deeply integrated into Apple’s operating systems and the apps people use every day, including the apps from our vast ecosystem of developers. Thousands of developers have already built integrations with Siri to let users ask for directions, manage a to-do list, send a message, or catch up on an audiobook. Siri AI is available in many languages, including English, French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish and will soon expand to support Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese. People around the world are turning to Siri AI to get things done every day, which means more customers can discover and use apps just by asking.

Today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, natural language, and more. So people can just ask for help in their own words, and Siri AI carries out any custom action you’ve built, from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order. For complex requests, we’re also introducing skills to let you teach Siri AI how to combine several actions into a single experience. And Siri AI can now surface any entity in the Spotlight semantic index, not just the ones that fit an existing schema.

We started rolling out these new capabilities across many Apple apps, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather, so users can do things like find a coffee shop they visited last week or archive files that haven’t been opened in over a year. There are many more actions available now as examples for you to reference. To see what you can do in each app, just ask Siri AI.

This developer beta offers a sneak peek at Siri AI app intents for developers. With this early Developer Preview, your app can work directly with Siri AI, giving you a first look at new ways to reach and serve your customers. This preview provides early access before first shipping to customers in a few months; and with submission to the App Store opening up in the spring, developers have time to explore, build, and help shape their experiences before launch. Try it out and share your feedback.

As you explore early, we will follow up with more details about the terms and usage policies for experiences enabled through Siri AI. More to share soon.

To learn more about the new APIs, how to use them, and how to evaluate your app’s experience with Siri AI, read new documentation. You can also connect with Apple engineers in Apple Intelligence Group Labs on November 4–5 to ask questions, get advice, and follow the discussion.

news.article_content_zh:
从今天开始，从 iOS 27.3、iPadOS 27.3、macOS 27.3 和 VisionOS 27.3 Beta 版开始，新的开发者预览版使任何开发者都可以将其应用程序与 Siri AI 集成，为企业和开发者提供接触和服务客户​​的新方式。

Siri AI 是 Siri 的全新版本，功能更加强大、更具对话性和个性化，旨在深度集成到 Apple 的操作系统和人们每天使用的应用程序中，包括来自我们庞大的开发者生态系统的应用程序。成千上万的开发者已经与 Siri 建立了集成，让用户可以询问方向、管理待办事项列表、发送消息或收听有声读物。 Siri AI 支持多种语言，包括英语、法语、日语、韩语、葡萄牙语和西班牙语，并将很快扩展到支持繁体中文、挪威语、土耳其语和越南语。世界各地的人们每天都在求助于 Siri AI 来完成工作，这意味着更多的客户只需询问即可发现和使用应用程序。

今天的预览版允许任何应用程序通过使用应用程序意图将其内容和操作直接引入 Siri AI，从而使所有应用程序更轻松地利用 Siri AI 的最新功能，包括个人上下文理解、屏幕感知、自然语言等。因此，人们只需用自己的话寻求帮助，Siri AI 就会执行您构建的任何自定义操作，从检查送货到预订再到下订单。对于复杂的请求，我们还引入了一些技能，让您可以教 Siri AI 如何将多个操作组合成一个体验。 Siri AI 现在可以显示 Spotlight 语义索引中的任何实体，而不仅仅是适合现有模式的实体。

我们开始在许多 Apple 应用程序中推出这些新功能，包括日历、文件、Finder、日记、邮件、地图、消息、音乐、笔记、照片、预览、提醒、Safari、快捷方式和天气，以便用户可以执行诸如查找上周访问过的咖啡店或归档一年多没有打开的文件等操作。现在还有更多操作示例可供您参考。要了解每个应用程序可以执行哪些操作，只需询问 Siri AI。

此开发者测试版让开发者可以一睹 Siri AI 应用意图。借助此早期开发者预览版，您的应用程序可以直接与 Siri AI 配合使用，让您首先了解接触和服务客户​​的新方法。此预览版提供了在几个月后首次发货给客户之前的早期访问；随着春季开放的 App Store 提交，开发人员有时间在发布前探索、构建和帮助塑造他们的体验。尝试一下并分享您的反馈。

当您尽早探索时，我们将跟进有关通过 Siri AI 实现的体验的条款和使用政策的更多详细信息。更多内容即将分享。

要了解有关新 API、如何使用它们以及如何评估应用程序使用 Siri AI 的体验的更多信息，请阅读新文档。您还可以于 11 月 4 日至 5 日与 Apple Intelligence Group Labs 的 Apple 工程师联系，提出问题、获取建议并关注讨论。

news.title: OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra designed a hardware device from scratch in under a week
news.title_en: OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra designed a hardware device from scratch in under a week
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
OpenAI's hardware team used GPT-6 Astra to design a device for the Codex coding agent in under a week, handling everything from the enclosure to the circuit board to the firmware. Several revision rounds were needed before production because the model didn't always account for manufacturing tolerances. A newer internal model scores significantly higher on OpenAI's engineering benchmark, though the company isn't sharing details.

The article OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra designed a hardware device from scratch in under a week appeared first on The Decoder.

news.content_snippet: OpenAI, Anthropic and other tech companies have vowed to protect Tuesday's elections from efforts to undermine democracy.

news.title: Rapid LLM development is outrunning the research meant to explain it, study finds
news.title_en: Rapid LLM development is outrunning the research meant to explain it, study finds
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Stanford researchers tested 50 widely cited claims about LLMs against 20 current models. 44 percent of the findings are already "expired," and another 34 percent have weakened significantly. The average lifespan is just 15.7 months. Claims about what models can't do expire fastest.

The article Rapid LLM development is outrunning the research meant to explain it, study finds appeared first on The Decoder.
news.content_snippet:
Stanford researchers tested 50 widely cited claims about LLMs against 20 current models. 44 percent of the findings are already "expired," and another 34 percent have weakened significantly. The average lifespan is just 15.7 months. Claims about what models can't do expire fastest.

The article Rapid LLM development is outrunning the research meant to explain it, study finds appeared first on The Decoder.
news.summary_en: Stanford researchers analyzed 50 widely cited claims about LLMs, finding that 44% are obsolete and 34% have significantly weakened, with an average shelf life of just 15.7 months. Claims about model limitations become irrelevant fastest, proving that LLM evolution is outpacing the pace of academic research.
news.title_zh: AI研究的寿命竟不足16个月
news.summary_zh: 斯坦福研究指出，由于AI迭代过快，近8成关于LLM能力的论文结论在短时间内即告“过期”或失效

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 斯坦福研究人员对比分析了50项关于大语言模型的权威研究，发现约44%的结论已完全失效，34%的结论效力显著减弱，平均有效期仅为15.7个月。其中，关于“模型不能做什么”的论断失效速度最快，反映出AI技术的进化速度已彻底碾压了学术界对其进行解释和归纳的能力。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Stanford researchers analyzed 50 widely cited claims about LLMs, finding that 44% are obsolete and 34% have significantly weakened, with an average shelf life of just 15.7 months. Claims about model limitations become irrelevant fastest, proving that LLM evolution is outpacing the pace of academic research.

elements_zh.why: 由于大语言模型更新换代过快，导致静态研究滞后于模型进化速度

elements_en.what: High obsolescence rate of AI research findings, with an average lifespan of only 15.7 months
elements_en.why: Rapid model iteration outpaces the pace of academic inquiry

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 在AI圈发论文简直是在玩‘打地鼠’，前脚刚论证模型智力天花板，后脚就被模型的新版本扇了脸。与其说是科研，不如说是在给不断进化、随时背刺人类常识的数字怪物写遗书。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Publishing AI research right now is like playing a game of 'Whac-A-Mole'—you prove a model's limits, and by the time it hits the printer, the next update has already made you look like a clown. It’s not so much science as it is writing obituaries for AI capabilities that are constantly evolving to spite us.

斯坦福大学的研究人员针对 20 个当前模型测试了 50 个被广泛引用的有关法学硕士的说法。 44% 的研究结果已经“过期”，另外 34% 的研究结果已显着减弱。平均寿命只有15.7个月。关于模型不能做什么的声明很快就会失效。

news.title: Apple’s latest watchOS beta includes its new always-on Audio Intelligence features
news.title_en: Apple’s latest watchOS beta includes its new always-on Audio Intelligence features
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content: Starting today, Siri can tune into the Apple Watch's mic with Audio Intelligence features that are available in the new watchOS 27.3 developer beta rolling out now. The two new additions are Siri Recap, which uses "ambient listening" to generate summaries of your conversation, and Live Rewind, which generates text transcripts of the last 15 seconds of audio your watch's mic detected.
news.content_snippet: Starting today, Siri can tune into the Apple Watch's mic with Audio Intelligence features that are available in the new watchOS 27.3 developer beta rolling out now. news.summary_en: Apple introduced 'Audio Intelligence' features in its latest watchOS developer beta, enabling Siri to generate conversation summaries and live transcriptions of the last 15 seconds of audio. This move aims to push AI dialogue management to the wrist, leveraging persistent microphone monitoring to enhance intelligent daily life tracking.

news.title: OpenAI says ChatGPT is catching up to Google in search
news.title_en: OpenAI says ChatGPT is catching up to Google in search
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
In many circles, "Ask Chat" has replaced "Google it," and that's reflected in a new announcement from OpenAI: the volume of search queries run through ChatGPT now equals 20 percent of the volume run through Google.

Adam Fry, OpenAI's consumer product lead for ChatGPT, made the announcement at a press event on Monday. He said the company defines a search as any time a user inputs a query that results in a web search, as opposed to tasks like defining a term or a simple how-to explanation. (Fry did not specify the source of the Google search volume number.)

But the game is "still awaiting approval," forcing the team to delay the release, according to a post from game director Alfred Kamon.
